notes: Checks run from the repo root. A check that runs its work in a container or on another host (docker exec, kubectl exec, ssh) needs a 'cleanup' command: a check killed at the gate cap takes only its local client with it, so the gate runs 'cleanup' after a timeout, with the same $MYSPEC_CHECK_RUN_ID the check saw. Have the check record its remote PID in a file named after $MYSPEC_CHECK_RUN_ID, and have 'cleanup' kill that PID's process group. In a linked worktree, a check that runs a container exec (docker exec, docker container exec, docker compose exec, docker-compose exec, podman exec, podman-compose exec) without -w/--workdir is refused as unverifiable: it runs in the container's mount of the checkout the container or compose project was started from, usually the main checkout, so it would not verify the worktree. Mount the worktree in the container and pass -w with its path there, or run the tool on the host. The gate trusts -w without verifying it, so it must name the worktree's mount. Better: describe the mount in a top-level 'containers' map, name -> {"mountSource": repo-relative directory the container mounts (usually "."), "mountTarget": absolute path it is mounted at inside the container}, and give the check "runIn": <name>. The gate then exports $MYSPEC_CHECK_WORKDIR, where this checkout's mountSource sits inside the container (mountTarget in the main checkout; mountTarget plus the worktree's path under the main checkout in a worktree nested under the mount), so one command is right in both: docker compose -p myapp exec -w "$MYSPEC_CHECK_WORKDIR" api make lint, or the same with podman exec or kubectl exec. Pin the compose project (-p, or a top-level name: in the compose file): compose otherwise names it after the directory it runs in, and from a worktree that is the worktree directory, so it finds no running service. Exec on the container by its name pins it too. A runIn check is not refused for its exec when it passes -w/--workdir or uses $MYSPEC_CHECK_WORKDIR; it is refused, not run, when the worktree is outside the mounted directory ("this worktree is not visible inside the container") or when runIn names a container 'containers' does not define. Give a check a non-empty 'diffCommand' when its plain 'command' already fails on the default branch: the gate runs 'diffCommand' instead, with $MYSPEC_BASE_REF exported as the merge base with the default branch. Scope the command to that range and guard it against an empty file set, e.g. files=$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMR $MYSPEC_BASE_REF -- '*.ts'); [ -z "$files" ] || npx eslint $files. Give a check "paths", a list of repo-relative globs, to run it only when a file this session wrote in the checkout matches one: '*' and '?' stay within one path segment, '**' as a whole segment spans any number of them, a trailing '/' means everything under it, and each glob matches the whole path from the repo root ('**/*.py' for any depth). A path git reports changed in the checkout (uncommitted, untracked, or against the base) also runs the check when it matches, because the session record misses rm, git revert and generated files. A required check skipped this way is named in the stop message. Without paths a check always runs, and so does every check when the session's writes are unknown. A polyglot pair: {"name": "API tests", "command": "docker compose -p myapp exec -w \"$MYSPEC_CHECK_WORKDIR/api\" api composer test", "runIn": "api", "paths": ["api/**"], "required": true} runs the PHP suite in a container, and {"name": "Web typecheck", "command": "npx tsc --noEmit -p web", "paths": ["web/**"], "required": true} runs the TypeScript check on the host, with "containers": {"api": {"mountSource": ".", "mountTarget": "/srv/app"}}.
